key_insight: Apparent learning gains in an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration agent largely disappeared after controlling for shared references, with no clear benefit from policy adaptation.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate migration agents with reference-disjoint tests and behavioral checks, because retrieval success and PostgreSQL acceptance do not establish correct migration.
method: Compared persistent memory and policy adaptation against no-memory and nearest-target copy baselines.
Audited reference overlap and reran evaluation with reference-grouped splits.
Tested real PL/SQL behavior, human-gated fixes, and retrieval stability as memory grew.
evidence_signal: Across four studies, 72% of the initial held-out units shared training references; on 103 leak-free units, the memory effect on reference conformity was 0.002 with an interval spanning zero [-0.008, 0.011].
watch_item: PostgreSQL acceptance is not semantic correctness: 10–22% of accepted units in the Oracle-grounded evaluation were behaviorally incorrect.
paper_title: Does a Self-Learning Migration Agent Learn? An Audited Evaluation of Evidence-Graded Experience Memory for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
